law_name: Income Tax Act (Zakon o porezu na dohodak), NN 115/2016 – 2017 tax reform
description: Adopted by parliament on 2 December 2016 as the centrepiece of the first Plenković government's tax reform and in force from 1 January 2017. It set two income-tax rates, 24% on an annual tax base of up to HRK 210,000 and 36% above it, and set the basic personal allowance at HRK 3,800 a month.
significance: Part of the tax reform package adopted by his first government in December 2016, in force from 2017.

law_name: Act on the Procedure of Extraordinary Administration in Companies of Systemic Importance for the Republic of Croatia ('Lex Agrokor'), NN 32/2017
description: Adopted on 6 April 2017 and in force the day after publication. It allows a court, at the request of a large indebted company and on the government's proposal, to open extraordinary administration and appoint an extraordinary commissioner who runs the group and negotiates a settlement with creditors. It was applied to the Agrokor food and retail group.
significance: Plenković said the law was drafted 'in a matter of weeks and adopted at literally the last minute' to prevent a chain of bankruptcies; the drafting with outside consultants led to the 2018 resignation of Deputy Prime Minister Martina Dalić and to conflict-of-interest proceedings (see polemics and justice).

law_name: Act ratifying the Council of Europe Convention on preventing and combating violence against women and domestic violence (Istanbul Convention), NN-MU 3/2018
description: Adopted by parliament on 13 April 2018. The act contains an interpretative declaration stating that Croatia considers the aim of the Convention to be the protection of women from all forms of violence, and that the Convention does not oblige it to introduce 'gender ideology' into its legal and educational systems or to change the constitutional definition of marriage.
significance: Fulfilled a commitment Plenković made in November 2016 despite opposition from conservative groups; the interpretative declaration was the government's response to those concerns.

law_name: Amendments to the Pension Insurance Act (Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o mirovinskom osiguranju), NN 115/2018, and their reversal, NN 102/2019
description: The amendments adopted on 7 December 2018 set the right to an old-age pension at 67 years of age and 15 years of contributions from 1 January 2033 (and early retirement at 62 with 35 years of contributions). After a trade-union referendum initiative, parliament adopted on 18 October 2019 new amendments restoring the old-age pension at 65 years of age and 15 years of contributions from 1 January 2020.
significance: The main element of the reform was withdrawn within a year, after about 700,000 signatures were collected for a referendum (see promises).

law_name: Act on the Reconstruction of Earthquake-Damaged Buildings in the City of Zagreb, Krapina-Zagorje County and Zagreb County, NN 102/2020
description: Adopted on 11 September 2020, after the 2020 Zagreb earthquake. It sets out the programme of reconstruction measures, establishes a Reconstruction Fund (Fond za obnovu) to prepare and carry out the reconstruction of damaged buildings, and requires the ministry, the Fund and public owners to publish regular information on spending.
significance: Legal basis of the post-earthquake reconstruction; Dnevnik Nova TV noted in October 2026 that the damage from the Zagreb and Banovina earthquakes was still being repaired.

law_name: Act on the Prevention of Conflicts of Interest (Zakon o sprječavanju sukoba interesa), NN 143/2021
description: Framework law adopted on 15 December 2021. It regulates the obligations of officials, asset declarations and the election and powers of the Commission for the Resolution of Conflicts of Interest.
significance: Adopted after court rulings had limited the Commission's power to rule on breaches of the general principles of office, which had been the basis of several findings against Plenković and his ministers; former Commission president Dalija Orešković said earlier drafts sought to remove some of the Commission's powers (Dnevnik Nova TV, 2021).

law_name: Act on the Introduction of the Euro as the Official Currency in the Republic of Croatia (Zakon o uvođenju eura kao službene valute), NN 57/2022
description: Adopted on 13 May 2022. It regulates the changeover from the kuna to the euro, including the rules for conversion at the fixed conversion rate, the exchange of cash, the period of dual circulation and the dual display of prices; its main provisions applied from the day the euro was introduced, 1 January 2023.
significance: Legal basis of Croatia's entry into the euro area, achieved on the date set by the government; Croatia joined the Schengen area the same day.

law_name: Act on Salaries in the Civil Service and Public Services (Zakon o plaćama u državnoj službi i javnim službama), NN 155/2023
description: Adopted on 15 December 2023 and in force from 1 January 2024. It sets a single system in which the basic salary is the product of the coefficient of the post and a base set by collective agreement, covering civil servants and public-service employees.
significance: Introduced a common pay system for the civil service and public services from 2024.

law_name: Amendments to the Criminal Code (Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Kaznenog zakona), NN 36/2024
description: Adopted on 14 March 2024. The amendments introduced the separate offence of aggravated murder of a woman (femicide, Article 111.a, at least ten years' imprisonment or long-term imprisonment) and Article 307.a, punishing judicial and police officials, defendants, lawyers, witnesses, experts and interpreters who disclose the content of non-public investigative or evidentiary actions with up to three years' imprisonment, with an exemption for journalistic work and for disclosures in a predominantly public interest.
significance: Article 307.a, dubbed 'Lex AP' by critics, was opposed by journalists' organisations and ARTICLE 19 as a threat to media freedom (see polemics).

law_name: Amendments to the Defence Act and the Act on Service in the Armed Forces (reintroduction of compulsory basic military training)
description: Passed by parliament on 24 October 2025. Men are called up in the calendar year in which they turn 19 for two months of basic military training in Knin, Slunj or Požega, paid about EUR 1,100 net a month and counted as pensionable service; conscientious objectors perform civilian service in civil protection or local government, and women may volunteer.
significance: Ended the suspension of conscription in force since 2008; the first intakes trained in 2026.
